name: Cavitation Pulse Carbine CPC-2 'Bends'
description:
The CPC-2 does not fire a traditional projectile. Instead, it discharges a focused column of superheated, electromagnetically compressed gas at pressures sufficient to induce localized cavitation in dense biological tissue — the same phenomenon that destroys the joints of deep-sea divers who ascend too rapidly, reproduced instantaneously at range. The discharge appears visually as a faint shimmer, almost invisible in daylight, with a sharp crack like snapping bamboo. At the point of impact, microscopic gas bubbles form and collapse violently within soft tissue, producing internal rupture without visible external trauma at low power settings. At higher settings, the effect is catastrophically visible.

Zheng-Dao's engineers developed the Bends by adapting industrial ultrasonic cavitation cleaning technology — originally used to strip contaminants from precision circuit components — into a directed-energy weapons platform. The core innovation is the Resonant Pressure Sheath, a conical emitter array at the muzzle that shapes the discharge into a coherent column rather than an expanding cone, preserving destructive pressure over distance. The carbine form factor is compact enough for vehicle use and close-quarters operation, which was the primary design brief from Zheng-Dao's infrastructure security division.

The weapon has two notable operational quirks. First, it is significantly more effective against targets with high fluid content — biological organisms, hydraulic systems, liquid-cooled electronics — and nearly useless against dry, rigid structures. Second, the discharge produces a subsonic resonance in the 18–22 Hz range that some operators report causes mild nausea and disorientation even in the shooter, earning it an unofficial reputation as a weapon that punishes careless use.
legality: Prohibited — classified as a directed biological harm emitter under GLMZ Statute 7.4.2
specifications:
discharge type: Superheated compressed gas column, electromagnetically shaped
effective range: 15m (full cavitation) / 60m (reduced-effect zone)
power settings: Three: Sublethal Disruption / Cavity Induction / Full Rupture
power source: Zheng-Dao Type-4 Bioelectric Cell, 40 discharges per cell
weight: 2.9 kg
dimensions: 490mm length, compact carbine profile
target effectiveness: High against biological and fluid-system targets; minimal effect on dry rigid materials
subsonic byproduct: 18–22 Hz resonance pulse, 3m radius around shooter
integrated systems: Pressure gauge, power-mode selector, muzzle sheath alignment indicator
tactical_use: Enforcement and extraction teams use the Bends primarily in confined, target-rich environments where over-penetration is a liability — server rooms, medical facilities, pressurized transit carriages. The Sublethal Disruption setting is favored for crowd control and detainee compliance, producing incapacitating internal pain without permanent damage. Full Rupture mode is documented in several high-profile corporate assassinations where the lack of visible external trauma allowed time of death to be obscured. The weapon's ineffectiveness against dry rigid structures means operators typically carry a conventional sidearm for dealing with barricades, locks, and armored targets.
cultural_context: The Bends occupies a deeply uncomfortable place in GLMZ's cultural landscape. Its prohibition stems not just from lethality but from the nature of the wounds it inflicts — internal, invisible, deniable — which has made it the weapon of choice for actors who need harm to look like something else. Zheng-Dao officially discontinued the CPC-2 following the Statute 7.4.2 ruling, but the discontinuation was widely understood as a paperwork exercise; production moved to unlicensed fabrication partners within six months. Among street-level fixers, offering someone 'a case of the Bends' has become idiom for a targeted, deniable hit.
known_users: Corrupt enforcement officers (confiscated units in circulation)
Corporate intelligence operatives requiring deniable lethality
story_hooks: A prominent GLMZ labor organizer is found dead with no visible wounds — the coroner's report is suppressed, but a street medic who saw the body recognizes the internal rupture pattern of a Bends discharge.
A shipment of Zheng-Dao Type-4 Bioelectric Cells is being moved through the port district — the cells are the right spec for the CPC-2, but the manifest lists them as medical imaging equipment.

An operator reports that their Bends has begun discharging at Full Rupture mode regardless of the power selector setting — and they need it traced to its fabrication batch before they can figure out if it's a fault or a deliberate modification.

A Zheng-Dao engineer who worked on the original CPC-2 project is offering to sell the Resonant Pressure Sheath schematics — but three other buyers are already in the bidding, and not all of them want the schematics to reach market.
